reply_text:
I found two forecasts by Suleyman from 2017 that count, plus one borderline item. All three come from news features that quote him, not from his own writing or a full question-and-answer transcript. I used all 12 searches and 3 of the 6 page openings.

**The two that count**
- **Eye-scan AI, 31 January 2017 (New Statesman).** The reporter writes that Suleyman says mass adoption is "a reasonable thing to expect over a five-year period." The sentence before is about AI grading eye scans better than a person, so that is almost certainly what he means. Only the eight quoted words are his. The rest is the reporter's paraphrase, and the interview may have been done in late 2016.
- **Healthcare in ten years, March 2017 (Digital Health).** He's quoted as saying DeepMind "wouldn't be in this if we didn't believe that in 10 years time we could radically transform healthcare." This is borderline. It reads partly as company ambition rather than a forecast about AI, and the page I opened showed no publication date (March 2017 comes from the web address). The same article has his comments on prices and payment models, which are business forecasts and are left out.

**What doesn't count for 2017**
- The essay "In 2018, AI will gain a moral compass" is his own writing, but it was published online on 5 January 2018. It also predicts growth in AI ethics work, not something AI itself will do. It goes under 2018.
- A December 2016 conference talk where he reportedly put general AI about 20 years away. I only saw that in search previews, so I didn't quote it.
- Every search with "2017" in it returned mostly 2025–2026 news about his 12–18-month job-automation forecast.

I found no 2017 statement from him about when AGI or superintelligence arrives, and none of my searches turned up a 2017 podcast, talk or essay in his own words.
